entries.name: Jomon people
entries.settlement: semi-sedentary villages of pit dwellings near coasts and nut groves
entries.beliefs: animism; fertility and mother-goddess figurines
entries.fell_by: gradual replacement by Yayoi rice farmers after c. 300 BCE
entries.notes: The world's oldest known pottery comes from this culture; Jomon means 'cord-marked'.

entries.name: Yayoi people
trade: Korean peninsula and Chinese bronze, iron and mirrors
entries.beliefs: rice fertility rites; ancestor veneration
entries.fell_by: evolved into Kofun-period chiefdoms
entries.notes: Named after the district in Tokyo where its pottery was found; rice farming arrived with migrants from Korea.

entries.name: Kofun culture
entries.settlement: chiefly centers around rulers in great keyhole tombs
trade: horses and iron from the Korean peninsula
entries.beliefs: ancestor and sun-line rulership
entries.fell_by: absorbed into the centralized Yamato state with Buddhism
entries.notes: Built the largest tombs in East Asia; Daisen Kofun (Nintoku's tomb) is among the world's biggest graves.

entries.name: Yamato state
entries.settlement: palace capitals that moved with each reign
crafts: imported Chinese and Korean writing and law
entries.beliefs: kami worship and the imperial sun-line
entries.fell_by: reorganized into a ritsuryo bureaucracy, settled in permanent capitals
entries.notes: Honcho Kōki-era rulers claimed descent from Amaterasu; Himiko of Yamatai is the earliest named ruler recorded by China.

entries.name: Asuka culture
entries.beliefs: Buddhism adopted alongside kami
entries.fell_by: superseded by the fixed Nara capital
entries.notes: Buddhism arrived with Baekje gifts in 538; Prince Shotoku's 'Seventeen-article constitution' fused Confucian ethics with Buddhism.

entries.name: Nara court
entries.settlement: grid capital on the Tang model
trade: Silk Road goods via China (Shosoin treasures)
entries.beliefs: state Buddhism with Shinto shrines
entries.fell_by: capital moved to Nagaoka then Heian-kyo in 794 to escape Buddhist politics
entries.notes: The Todaiji Great Buddha was the largest bronze statue in the world for centuries; the Shosoin storehouse keeps 8th-century Silk Road treasures intact.

entries.name: Heian court aristocracy
entries.settlement: grid capital around the imperial palace
entries.beliefs: Pure Land Buddhism, Esoteric Shingon and Tendai, kami
entries.fell_by: estate collapse and the rise of provincial warrior power; Gempei War 1180-1185
entries.notes: Home of The Tale of Genji; kana script made literary culture a court art led by women.

entries.name: Kamakura samurai
entries.settlement: fortified coastal capital, provincial manor houses
trade: Mongol invasions 1274 and 1281 failed at Hakata Bay
entries.beliefs: Zen Buddhism, Pure Land, martial honour
entries.fell_by: Ashikaga Takauji overthrew the shogunate in 1333 and 1336
entries.notes: First warrior government; samurai values of duty and loyalty were codified under shoguns, not the emperor.

entries.name: Muromachi (Ashikaga) culture
entries.beliefs: Zen Buddhism patronized by warrior elite
entries.fell_by: Onin War 1467-1477 shattered central authority; warlords supplanted shoguns
entries.notes: The Ashikaga shoguns turned Zen aesthetics into canonical Japanese arts despite near-continuous civil war.

entries.name: Sengoku daimyo
entries.settlement: hilltop castles and planned castle towns (jōkamachi)
trade: red-seal ship trade to Southeast Asia
entries.beliefs: Zen, Pure Land (Ikkō-ikki revolts), Jesuit-introduced Christianity
entries.fell_by: Sekigahara 1600 and Tokugawa unification
entries.notes: A century of inter-domain war; firearms arrived at Tanegashima in 1543 and changed Japanese warfare overnight.

entries.name: Tokugawa shogunate
trade: Ryukyu and Matsumae domains as channels
entries.beliefs: Neo-Confucian state ideology, Shinto, Pure Land and Nichiren Buddhism
entries.fell_by: Commodore Perry's black ships 1853; Meiji Restoration 1868
entries.notes: Two and a half centuries of peace under strict class order; closed the country to all Europeans except the Dutch at Dejima.

entries.name: Edo chōnin (townspeople)
entries.settlement: narrow-fronted machiya townhouses along canal streets
entries.beliefs: popular Shinto and Buddhism; pragmatic merchant ethics
entries.fell_by: Meiji class abolition 1871
entries.notes: Merchant and artisan culture that invented ukiyo-e, kabuki and sushi; Yoshiwara and Genroku are its symbols.

entries.name: Meiji modernizers
entries.settlement: Tokyo as capital; modern ports and rail towns
entries.beliefs: State Shinto; 'civilization and enlightenment' ideology
entries.fell_by: Taisho era and instability; militarism followed after 1926
entries.notes: Abolished the samurai class, built railways and a conscript army; by 1905 Japan defeated Russia by sea and land.

entries.name: Kirishitan (Japanese Christians)
entries.settlement: port towns in Kyushu; remote hideout villages
entries.beliefs: Roman Catholic Christianity (suppressed); later Kakure Kirishitan folk syncretism
entries.fell_by: Tokugawa suppression edicts; Shimabara-Amakusa rebellion 1637-1638; sakoku
entries.notes: Hidden Christians practiced in secret for 220 years; 'discover' of them at Oura Cathedral 1865 stunned the world.

entries.name: Ainu (Aynu)
trade: Wajin Japanese: herring, sea otter, kelp (Chitose trade through Matsumae)
entries.beliefs: animism; kamuy spirits; bear ceremony (iyomante); oral epics (yukar)
entries.notes: Indigenous people of northern Japan; recognized as indigenous only in 2008; language nearly extinct.

entries.name: Nivkh (Gilyak)
entries.region: Sakhalin Island and lower Amur basin
entries.beliefs: animism; clan spirits; bear-sending ritual
entries.notes: Isolated 'Paleo-Asiatic' language unrelated to neighbors; several thousand speakers remain.

entries.name: Ryukyuan (Shuri court)
entries.settlement: walled capital at Shuri; harbor towns
entries.beliefs: Ryukyuan folk religion and noro priestesses
entries.fell_by: Satsuma invasion 1609 reduced independence; annexed by Japan 1879
entries.notes: Maritime middleman kingdom linking China, Japan and Southeast Asia; distinct Okinawan languages survive.

entries.name: Miyako Islanders
entries.beliefs: Ryukyuan folk religion, animist sea spirits
entries.notes: Distinct Miyako language; famous for the 1700s-born ballad tradition and for walled coral-stone villages.

entries.name: Hachijō Islanders
trade: Edo and Tokyo via ship (historically intermittent)
entries.beliefs: Japanese folk Shinto and volcano veneration
entries.notes: An island of internal exiles; their isolated dialect preserves archaic Japanese unintelligible elsewhere.

entries.name: Ogasawara (Bonin) Islanders
entries.beliefs: Christian, Shinto and Japanese folk blends
entries.notes: Descendants of 1830 colonists from Honolulu of European, Polynesian and Native American origin mixed with Japanese settlers; speak Ogasawara dialect.

entries.name: Taiwanese Austronesian peoples
entries.beliefs: animism; ancestor and headhunting rites; Christianity (20th c.)
entries.notes: Taiwan is the Austronesian homeland; sixteen recognized indigenous nations live here, source population for Pacific expansion.

entries.name: Amis (Pangcah)
trade: Han Chinese at Hualien and Taitung markets
entries.beliefs: mother-house worship; harvest festival (kiluma'an); Christianity
entries.notes: The largest indigenous nation in Taiwan; matrilineal kinship and an autumn harvest festival define village life.

entries.name: Paiwan
entries.beliefs: five-paced snake as noble patron ancestor
entries.notes: Known for chiefly rank society, twin-tailed five-paced-snake iconography and finely carved house posts.

entries.name: Atayal (Tayal)
entries.beliefs: ancestor spirits (utux); headhunting formerly central to bravery rites
entries.notes: Famed warriors and tattooed weavers; the 1930 Wushe revolt was a famous anti-Japanese uprising.

entries.name: Bunun (Bunuaz)
entries.beliefs: celestial and ancestor deities
entries.notes: Their Pasiputput choral song is an eight-part harmony once used to warn of earthquakes by octave overtones.

entries.name: Tao (Yami)
entries.beliefs: anito sea spirits; flying-fish season rituals (a swimming carried on to spawn)
entries.notes: The only sea-going canoe culture in Taiwan; whole communities migrate for flying-fish season.

entries.name: Siraya (Pingpu) plains people
entries.beliefs: Tapaghaw ancestral goddess; eight-year Night Ceremony
entries.fell_by: absorbed into Han Chinese settlement after Qing takeover 1683
entries.notes: Plains nations were 'raw' subjects to the Dutch and 'cooked' subjects to Qing; Siraya is now revived with a written orthography.

entries.name: Li people (Hlai)
trade: sea trade with Vietnam and Guangdong
entries.beliefs: animism; boat-shaped house as ancestral womb
entries.notes: Indigenous Austronesian-related people of Hainan; their woven heirlooms inspired the ikat tradition across Southeast Asia.

entries.name: Miao (Hmong) of Hainan
entries.beliefs: ancestor spirits (dab)
entries.notes: Migrated to Hainan in the Ming-Qing era to flee mainland warfare and land hunger; keep Hmong mountain dress and batik.

entries.name: Tanka boat people
entries.region: South China coasts and rivers (Pearl River delta, Fujian, coastal islands)
entries.settlement: villages of sampans on rivers and harbors
entries.beliefs: Matsu (sea goddess) worship; syncretic folk Buddhism
entries.notes: Officially registered as 'boat dwellers' and historically denied land ownership; now largely ashore, speak Cantonese and Min.

entries.name: Hokkien maritime merchants (Quanzhou)
entries.region: Quanzhou and the Fujian coast, Ryukyu and Taiwan entrepots
entries.settlement: walled port cities with foreign quarters
trade: porcelain and silk out, spices and silver in
entries.beliefs: Chinese folk religion, Mazu sea cult, Islam (Quanzhou Muslim quarter), Buddhism
entries.fell_by: haijin sea ban and Ming-Qing isolation; Zheng family carried on
entries.notes: Quanzhou under the Song and Yuan was arguably the world's busiest port; Ibn Battuta called it one of the greatest.

entries.name: Wokou (East Asian pirates)
entries.region: Coasts of China, Korea, Japan and offshore islands
entries.beliefs: mixed; crews of Japanese, Chinese, Korean and even Portuguese
entries.fell_by: Ming suppression campaigns and 1555-1567 bans; finally Qi Jiguang's victories
entries.notes: 'Dwarf pirates'; mostly Chinese smugglers with Japanese, Korean and Portuguese crews, not just Japanese.

entries.name: Tamna kingdom (Jeju)
crafts: basalt stone carving (tol hareubang grandfather stones)
entries.beliefs: shamanism; three founder demigods from holes in the ground (Samseonghyeol)
entries.fell_by: annexed by Goryeo 1105; rebellions suppressed 1273 (Mongol-era)
entries.notes: Home of the haenyeo, women who free-dive for abalone and conch without oxygen gear; UNESCO-listed intangible heritage since 2016.

entries.name: Dutch Formosa (VOC Taiwan)
entries.settlement: walled fort at Tainan; Dutch compound and market town
entries.beliefs: Dutch Calvinism; mission to native Siraya villages
entries.fell_by: Zheng Chenggong (Koxinga) conquered the island 1661-1662
entries.notes: The VOC taxed Siraya and Han farmers heavily; mission schools produced the first Romanized Siraya manuscripts.

entries.name: Zheng Ming Kingdom (Koxinga's Taiwan)
entries.settlement: garrison towns around Tainan; Fujian-style villages
entries.beliefs: Ming loyalist Confucianism and folk religion
entries.fell_by: Qing navy defeated the Zheng clan in 1683; Taiwan annexed to Qing
entries.notes: Last foothold of Ming dynasty loyalists; built the first Confucian academy on Taiwan in 1665.
